title: Policy translation layer and sidecar-less authorization middleware for API/runtime/console
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver an RBAC v2 policy translation and evaluation layer plus a thin, sidecar-less authorization middleware that can be embedded in API gateway, runtime worker, and console backend paths. This ticket covers the policy normalization pipeline, a compact decision cache keyed for high-cardinality request attributes, audit hooks with full per-decision context, and SSO/SAML group-to-role reconciliation integrations for console admin sync.

Problem statement: Our current authorizer surface is fragmented (console vs API vs runtime) and imposes either high latency (RPC to external PDP) or operational complexity (sidecars). RBAC v2 introduces richer role bindings and conditional rules that need a performant local evaluation strategy while preserving centralized policy lifecycle (versioning, rollouts, audits).

Proposal summary:
- Policy translation layer: compile RBAC v2 JSON/YAML into an optimized decision graph (predicates and actions) and a small predicate bytecode that can be executed in-process. Include a stable hash and semantic version to allow safe cache invalidation and rollouts.
- Evaluation engine: A deterministic, JIT-friendly evaluator with short-circuiting, partial-eval for common bindings, and a small LRU decision cache keyed on (policy_version, principal_fingerprint, resource_fingerprint, action). Include metrics for cache hit/miss, eviction causes, and per-decision timing. Target median eval time < 3ms in warm path.
- Sidecar-less middleware adapters: provide lightweight middleware modules for the API gateway (Go), runtime worker pool (Rust), and console backend (Node). Each adapter handles: extraction of auth attributes, evaluation call into the in-process evaluator, audit event emission, and fallback behavior.
- Audit streaming: emit structured audit events (immutable) for every decision to Kafka with fields: request_id, actor, resource, action, decision, policy_version, trace_id, evaluation_time_ms, and any matched predicates. Ensure events are redact-safe for PII and can be subsampled for high-volume endpoints.
- SSO/SAML sync: add a reconciliation layer that maps SAML group attributes to RBAC v2 role bindings and performs differential updates to internal role assignment indexes. Include an admin endpoint in console for conflict resolution and manual binding overrides.
- Rollout plan: start with console-only canary (5% of orgs), then API gateway async endpoints (20%), then runtime hot path. Provide a safe-fail policy (default to deny-with-logging) and an emergency override switch per-org in the control plane.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Evaluator produces identical decisions to the canonical PDP for a representative policy corpus and test set.
- Median evaluation time < 3ms on target CPU profile with cache warm, P95 < 15ms.
- Audit events reach Kafka and are queryable in the incident dashboards; schema validated.
- Console admin can view role mappings derived from SAML and manually resolve conflicts in the UI.
- Can be rolled out to 5% of orgs with no elevated error rate and a clear rollback path.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Local evaluation increases the attack surface for policy bugs; mitigation: deterministic test harness, nightly differential checks, and mandatory security review.
- Cache staleness: address via policy_versioned keys and short TTLs for attribute-derived keys.
- SAML group explosion: use sampled sync and incremental reconciliation to avoid spikes.

Testing plan: unit tests for translation correctness, property tests for evaluator equivalence with canonical PDP, load tests for evaluation latency and cache behavior, end-to-end canary with synthetic orgs, and manual QA of console admin flows.

Artifacts: design doc, benchmarking scripts, and initial PoC evaluators attached below.
